value: Can the Higgs field be a condensate of pairs of fermions, as the state of a superconductor is a condensate of pairs of electrons? We study this question in a model built on an algebraic structure, the Lorentz super-loop: the bi-octonions of unit norm, a Moufang loop (a set with a product that has an identity and inverses but is not associative). It contains the Lorentz group $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ and eight spinor charges, which are carried by an isodoublet $\Psi$ of Dirac spinors. We first show, with worked examples, how these objects arise, and why pairs of two members of $\Psi$ form isospin triplets, so that a condensate of $\Psi$ alone cannot be the Higgs doublet of the Standard Model. We then give $\Psi$ the hypercharge $\frac14$, add two singlet Dirac fields $\chi$ and $\chi'$ with the hypercharges $\frac14$ and $-\frac34$, and let a contact interaction bind a member of $\Psi$ to a singlet in a pair of spin zero. The two pair fields form a bidoublet of $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R$ (a $2\times2$ matrix of fields on which the two groups act from the left and from the right) with the quantum numbers of two Higgs doublets. In five mean-field methods (Hubbard-Stratonovich with three decouplings, Kohn-Sham, and Cornwall-Jackiw-Tomboulis) the ground state is the custodial vacuum, which keeps the symmetry that protects the ratio of the $W$ and $Z$ masses: it breaks $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ to the $U(1)$ of the electric charge, keeps the photon massless and gives $\rho=1$. Setting its scale to $v=246.22$~GeV puts the momentum cutoff at 2.2\mbox{--}2.4~TeV. The amplitude mode, the oscillation of the size of the condensate and the candidate for the Higgs boson, is a composite scalar bound below the threshold of two quasi-particles. Where only the pairing acts, the linear response has the closed form of the theory of Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer and places the mode exactly at the pair self-energy (the gap parameter of that theory): $M_H/v=7.967$, 16 times the measured $m_H/v=0.5082$, and over a scan of the coupling from 1.02 to 3 times its critical value, with two masses of the fields, the ratio is at least \ensuremath{4.892}. A custodial triplet of massive scalars and a Goldstone boson of the particle number come with it. The superfluid therefore has the quantum numbers of the Higgs field and gives the $W$ and $Z$ bosons their masses, but in the mean field its amplitude mode is far too heavy. We outline how gravitation will enter through E.~A.~Lord's gauge theory of the local change of spinor representation.
